muse-calliope: Muse of epic poetry, the eldest
muse-euterpe: Muse of music, often with a flute
titan-oceanus: Titan of the great world-river that circles the Earth
titan-coeus: Titan of intellect, grandfather of the twins born on Delos
titan-crius: Titan linked to the constellations, the least-known of the twelve
titan-hyperion: Titan of heavenly light, father of the Sun, Moon and Dawn
titan-iapetus: Titan father of Atlas and Prometheus
titan-theia: Titaness of sight and shining light
titan-rhea: Titaness mother of the Olympians who tricked her husband with a stone
titan-themis: Titaness of divine law, with scales
titan-mnemosyne: Titaness of memory, mother of the Muses
titan-phoebe: Titaness of prophecy, grandmother of the twins born on Delos
titan-tethys: Titaness of fresh water, wife of the world-river
titan-cronus: Titan king who swallowed his children
olympian-zeus: King of the gods, wielder of thunderbolts
olympian-hera: Queen of the gods, goddess of marriage
olympian-poseidon: God of the sea, with a trident
olympian-demeter: Goddess of the harvest, mother of Persephone
olympian-athena: Goddess of wisdom, born from her father's head
olympian-apollo: God of music, light and prophecy
olympian-artemis: Goddess of the hunt and the moon
olympian-aphrodite: Goddess of love, born from sea foam
olympian-hephaestus: Blacksmith god of fire and the forge
